articles.title: Peacemaker with a warning to annihilate: The major contradictions in Trump's UN speech
articles.description: Trump used much of his address to the General Debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly to list his achievements, much as he did a year ago when he cast himself as the standout contender for the Nobel Peace Prize. This year, though, the prize went unmentioned. Instead, his tone hardened, with attacks on the International Criminal Court (ICC), the UN's climate agenda and Unesco.

articles.title: Karnataka man 'murdered' in UAE, body cut into 9 pieces; wife, son untraceable
articles.description: A man from Kundapur, Alwin, was reported missing after last contacting his family in July. His family became suspicious after receiving unusual text messages from his phone, which he rarely used. After his body was discovered in Sharjah, they received a death certificate and filed various complaints. Alwin's wife and son remain uncontactable amid ongoing investigations. Udupi police await official confirmation of the incident from relevant authorities.

articles.title: UP man kills wife, 2 priests, takes 3 children hostage; shot dead after 7-hour standoff
articles.description: A police encounter resulted in the death of Arvind Singh after he refused to surrender during a standoff. During the incident, he was holding his three children hostage, leading to a police operation. Arvind had killed his wife and two priests following a dispute concerning a religious ritual at home. His eight-year-old son was also critically injured and later died from his injuries.

articles.title: LSR cancels classes, goes online after Kalkaji Mandir gang rape case
articles.description: Lady Shri Ram College cancelled regular classes and shifted them online after a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped at Aastha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir. Police said three men, posing as policemen, allegedly separated the girl from her male friend and assaulted her in a secluded area. All three accused have been arrested, while police are investigating the incident and checking for possible links to other cases.

articles.title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex jumps over 200 points; NSE Nifty50 trades above 23,400
articles.full_text: BSE Sensex is trading in green in opening trade, with Bajaj Finance rising 2.03% to Rs 1,029.50 and Bajaj Finserv gaining 1.53% to Rs 1,853. Tata Steel advanced 1.25% to Rs 187, while UltraTech Cement and Larsen & Toubro both climbed 0.89% to Rs 11,095 and Rs 3,904.55, respectively. Asian Paints rose 0.82% to Rs 2,464.35, followed by Kotak Bank at 0.63% to Rs 415.10 and Adani Ports at 0.61% to Rs 1,801. Titan gained 0.48% to Rs 4,933.50, while SBI and Power Grid rose 0.46% and 0.45% to Rs 990.70 and Rs 267.20, respectively. ITC gained 0.42% to Rs 266.15, while Indigo rose 0.38% to Rs 5,038.90. Hindustan Unilever and NTPC added 0.33% and 0.31% to Rs 1,941.45 and Rs 328, respectively. Bharti Airtel also advanced 0.31% to Rs 1,822.65. Reliance Industries rose 0.14% to Rs 1,243.80, while Sun Pharma gained 0.12% to Rs 1,846.30. Maruti edged up 0.07% to Rs 12,199, HCL Tech gained 0.04% to Rs 1,270.45 and Trent was almost flat, rising 0.01% to Rs 2,773.90. Rupee strengthened 16 paise to close at 95.62 against the US dollar in the previous trading session, supported by a sharp decline in crude oil prices, improved global risk sentiment and hopes of diplomatic talks to resolve the US-Iran war. The Indian currency opened at 95.75 and gained ground during the session to touch 95.55 against the dollar before settling at 95.62. The currency had closed at 95.78 in the previous session after appreciating 18 paise. The dollar index was trading at 100.34, down 0.08%, while US Treasury yields also declined after reports around possible diplomatic developments. Anuj Choudhary of Mirae Asset Sharekhan said the rupee was expected to trade with a positive bias, with USD-INR spot price seen in a 95.30-95.80 range. Benchmark indices ended the previous session in red, with BSE Sensex declining 329.91 points, or 0.44%, to settle at 74,529.08, while NSE Nifty fell 85.30 points, or 0.36%, to end at 23,329. Sensex had lost as much as 435.28 points, or 0.58%, during the session, touching 74,423.71. Bajaj Finserv, Trent, Bajaj Finance, Sun Pharma, Tata Consultancy Services and UltraTech Cement were among the major laggards on the 30-share index. Eternal, InterGlobe Aviation, Titan and Tata Steel were among the gainers. The domestic benchmarks declined despite a positive global market trend and lower crude oil prices, with IT, financials and capital goods stocks weighing on the indices. Foreign institutional investors also remained sellers, offloading equities worth Rs 3,809.99 crore on a net basis.

articles.title: Oil prices ease as Saudi restores key pipeline, traders optimistic on US-Iran talks
articles.description: Oil prices have dropped below $100 a barrel due to Saudi Arabia restarting crude supply operations. Diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict have also contributed to easing market pressure. US crude inventories increased by 1.8 million barrels in the past week, contrary to analysts' expectations. Iraq is reportedly increasing its oil exports, signaling a shift in regional supply dynamics.

articles.title: Five Indiana engineering students built a 12-hour wearable that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles beyond a cane or guide dog
articles.description: Rose-Hulman students have developed a remarkable wearable device tailored for visually impaired individuals. This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback. With a remarkable twelve-hour battery life on a single charge, this device empowers users with greater independence. The project's goal is to enhance the day-to-day experiences of those with vision impairments.

articles.title: Tom Cruise never reads his scripts before accepting role
articles.description: Tom Cruise has opened up about his unique approach to scripts, stating that he has them read aloud to him rather than reading them independently. He argues that this technique helps capture the director's intent and spot potential story flaws. Furthermore, Cruise actively collaborates with directors on vital aspects of filmmaking, such as lighting and cinematographic choices.
